test_cases.description: Four-tier cascade resolves a known glossary term
test_cases.user_prompt: Ask todd about the PSR for oracle
test_cases.setup_context: Glossary contains: todd -> Todd Martinez (Finance lead, importance 55), PSR -> Pipeline Status Report (importance 60), oracle -> Oracle Systems deal (importance 45). Taxonomy has no matching entries.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill decodes all three terms: todd -> Todd Martinez (Finance lead), PSR -> Pipeline Status Report, oracle -> Oracle Systems deal. Tier 1 (taxonomy) checked first, falls through to Tier 2 (glossary) where all three resolve. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 needed.

test_cases.description: Lifecycle filtering skips sunset entries and flags probationary ones
test_cases.user_prompt: What's the status on the phoenix migration and the aurora project?
test_cases.setup_context: memory/projects/phoenix.md exists with importance 25 (probationary). memory/projects/aurora.md exists with importance 8 (sunset). Glossary has no matching entries.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Phoenix is returned with (fading) flag since importance 25 is probationary (10-39). Aurora is skipped/not returned since importance 8 is below sunset threshold (<10). Skill suggests confirming Phoenix is still active.

test_cases.description: Fuzzy matching resolves partial terms
test_cases.user_prompt: Check with todd about the phoen project
test_cases.setup_context: Glossary contains: todd -> Todd Martinez. memory/projects/phoenix.md exists with importance 50.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill resolves 'phoen' to 'Phoenix' via fuzzy/partial matching. Todd resolves via glossary. Both terms decoded before acting on request.

test_cases.description: Tier 4 ask-user fires when term not found, checks pending.json
test_cases.user_prompt: Send the TPS report to Jenkins
test_cases.setup_context: No glossary entry for TPS or Jenkins. memory/pending.json contains {"TPS": {"first_seen": "2026-03-01"}}. No taxonomy match.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill checks all tiers, finds nothing for TPS and Jenkins. Before asking user, checks pending.json and finds TPS was seen before. Output says something like 'I've seen TPS mentioned before but don't have a definition yet. Can you clarify?' For Jenkins, asks user directly since it's not in pending either.

test_cases.description: Recall boost mechanic strengthens recalled entries
test_cases.user_prompt: Who is todd?
test_cases.setup_context: Glossary contains: todd -> Todd Martinez (importance 45). memory/people/todd-martinez.md exists (importance 45).

isolation_correctness.assertion: After resolving todd, the skill notes that recalled entries get +5 importance boost. The boost-on-recall mechanic is mentioned or applied. Cross-reference from glossary to people file is noted.

test_cases.description: Context assembly combines multiple tiers
test_cases.user_prompt: Tell me about todd and the billing module
test_cases.setup_context: Glossary: todd -> Todd Martinez. memory/people/todd-martinez.md exists with details about role, preferences, and projects. Taxonomy: products contains WebApp, modules contains Billing.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill combines Tier 1 (taxonomy resolves 'Billing' as a module) with Tier 2 (glossary resolves 'todd') and Tier 3 (deep memory provides full Todd profile). Assembled context includes both the person profile and the validated module name.

test_cases.description: After decoding terms, skill suggests downstream consumer relevance
test_cases.user_prompt: Ask todd about the PSR for oracle
test_cases.setup_context: All terms resolvable in glossary/deep memory.

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: After decoding, output mentions that resolved context is available for Product Forge card enrichment and/or Report Forge scoping. At minimum, acknowledges downstream plugins exist.

isolation_correctness.assertion: All three terms decoded correctly via tiered lookup.

test_cases.description: Memory-first resolution works as workspace-level behavior
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a story for the PSR dashboard
test_cases.setup_context: PSR exists in glossary (Pipeline Status Report, importance 60). This prompt would normally trigger Product Forge, but memory-management should fire first to decode PSR.

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: Skill triggers on unrecognized shorthand 'PSR' and resolves it before any downstream action. The description mentions decoding workplace shorthand — this should activate even when the user's primary intent is a Product Forge action.

isolation_correctness.assertion: PSR resolved to Pipeline Status Report via glossary lookup.

test_cases.description: Lifecycle filtering removal notifies about downstream impact
test_cases.user_prompt: What about the legacy SOAP integration?
test_cases.setup_context: memory/projects/soap-integration.md exists with importance 8 (sunset).

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: When the entry is filtered out as sunset, the skill notes that downstream content (Product Forge cards, Report Forge reports) referencing this integration may need reviewing.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Entry correctly identified as sunset (importance < 10) and skipped or flagged accordingly.

test_cases.description: Taxonomy query returns product list
test_cases.user_prompt: What products do we have?
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy contains: products = [WebApp, MobileApp, API Platform].

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill calls forge memory get-taxonomy products, returns the full list. Output formatted as taxonomy result with source noted as forge-lib managed.

test_cases.description: Person query searches knowledge entries
test_cases.user_prompt: Who is Maya?
test_cases.setup_context: Knowledge entry exists: person type, name Maya Chen, role Engineering Manager, team Platform Team.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill calls forge memory query-knowledge --type person, finds Maya in results, returns full profile with source path noted.

test_cases.description: Glossary term lookup via knowledge query
test_cases.user_prompt: What does PSR mean?
test_cases.setup_context: Knowledge entry exists: glossary type, term PSR, definition Pipeline Status Report.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill extracts 'PSR' as search keyword, queries glossary entries, returns definition. Output includes the term expansion and any usage context.

test_cases.description: Not-found triggers remember suggestion
test_cases.user_prompt: Tell me about the Zenith project
test_cases.setup_context: No taxonomy, knowledge, or context file matches for 'Zenith'.

isolation_correctness.assertion: After searching all three tiers and finding nothing, skill outputs 'I don't have that in memory yet' and offers to transition to /memory:remember workflow.

test_cases.description: Partial matches suggest related entries
test_cases.user_prompt: Tell me about the mobile project
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy has MobileApp product. Knowledge has a project 'mobile-redesign'. No exact match for 'mobile project'.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill finds partial matches in both taxonomy (MobileApp) and knowledge (mobile-redesign). Presents both as related entries and asks 'Did you mean one of these?'

test_cases.description: Tiered search uses progressive disclosure — stops at first tier with results
test_cases.user_prompt: What teams exist?
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy contains: teams = [Platform Team, Finance Team, Product Team]. Knowledge also has team-related person entries.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill finds the answer at Tier 1 (taxonomy) and returns it. Does NOT redundantly search Tier 2/3 since the query was fully answered. Output notes this is forge-lib managed.

test_cases.description: Recall of project info suggests Product Forge card creation
test_cases.user_prompt: Tell me about the Phoenix project
test_cases.setup_context: memory/projects/phoenix.md exists with full project details. No Product Forge card exists for Phoenix.

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: After presenting Phoenix project info, output suggests: 'Would you like to create a Product Forge card for this project?' or references /product-forge:create.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Phoenix project details returned correctly from knowledge query.

test_cases.description: Substantial recall results suggest Report Forge generation
test_cases.user_prompt: What do we know about the payments integration?
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy has 'Stripe' integration. Knowledge has project 'payments-overhaul' and person entries for payment team members. Rich context available.

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: After presenting substantial knowledge about payments, output suggests: 'There's enough context here to generate a focused report with /report-forge:generate' or similar.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Multi-source results assembled from taxonomy (Stripe integration) and knowledge (project + people). Cross-references noted.

test_cases.description: Recall of person info suggests enriching related tasks/cards
test_cases.user_prompt: Who is Todd?
test_cases.setup_context: Knowledge entry: person Todd Martinez, Finance lead, owns PSR process.

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: After presenting Todd's profile, output suggests person is available for Product Forge card enrichment or Tasks Forge task assignment context.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Todd's full profile returned with role, team, and context details.

test_cases.description: Exact taxonomy match resolves correctly
test_cases.user_prompt: Write a story for the billing module in WebApp
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy: products = [WebApp], modules = [Billing, Authentication, Notifications].

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill queries forge memory get-taxonomy, resolves 'WebApp' to product and 'billing module' to Billing module. Canonical names used: 'WebApp' and 'Billing'.

test_cases.description: Fuzzy/informal reference resolves to canonical name
test_cases.user_prompt: Create something for the mobile app
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy: products = [MobileApp, WebApp, API Platform].

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill resolves 'the mobile app' to 'MobileApp' via fuzzy, case-insensitive matching. Canonical name 'MobileApp' used in output.

test_cases.description: Unknown value triggers add suggestion with three options
test_cases.user_prompt: This is for the Nexus platform
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy: products = [WebApp, MobileApp, API Platform]. 'Nexus' not present.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill flags 'Nexus' as not in product taxonomy. Offers three options: 'Should I add it? / Use it anyway / Enter different value'. If user confirms, calls forge memory set-taxonomy products --add 'Nexus'.

test_cases.description: Missing taxonomy gracefully degrades to freeform
test_cases.user_prompt: This card is for the billing module
test_cases.setup_context: No taxonomy exists (memory system not initialized).

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill accepts 'billing' as freeform value without blocking. Informs user: 'Run /memory:setup-org to configure your taxonomy'. After workflow, offers to add the value.

test_cases.description: Taxonomy suggestion presents numbered list of options
test_cases.user_prompt: Which product should this story be for?
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy: products = [WebApp, MobileApp, API Platform].

isolation_correctness.assertion: Skill queries taxonomy and presents a numbered list: '1. WebApp 2. MobileApp 3. API Platform [Enter number or name]'. Accepts both number and name as input.

test_cases.description: Taxonomy addition confirms downstream Product Forge impact
test_cases.user_prompt: Add WebApp to our product taxonomy
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy exists but WebApp not yet present.

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: After adding WebApp, output confirms: 'Product Forge cards will now validate against this product name when creating or updating cards.' Names Product Forge specifically.

isolation_correctness.assertion: WebApp added via forge memory set-taxonomy products --add 'WebApp'. Confirmation shows the addition succeeded.

test_cases.description: Resolution consistency with Product Forge product-context
test_cases.user_prompt: Write a story for billing stuff in the mobile app for Acme
test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy: products = [MobileApp], modules = [Billing], clients = [Acme Corp].

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: Resolved terms match what Product Forge product-context would produce: 'billing stuff' -> Billing, 'the mobile app' -> MobileApp, 'Acme' -> Acme Corp. No inconsistency between org-context and product-context resolution.

isolation_correctness.assertion: All three informal references resolved to canonical taxonomy names via fuzzy matching.

test_cases.description: Taxonomy rename notes downstream impact on existing content

test_cases.setup_context: Taxonomy: modules = [Payments, Authentication, Notifications]. Existing Product Forge cards reference 'Payments'.

ecosystem_awareness.assertion: After rename, output notes: 'Existing Product Forge cards referencing Payments should be reviewed. Existing tasks with this module should be checked.' Acknowledges downstream propagation impact.

isolation_correctness.assertion: Old value removed and new value added via forge memory set-taxonomy. Rename completed successfully.
